The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 702eacef09cb6165), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 23-24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Fix any finite list of output derivative orders, including an exterior base buffer Nb. For every fixed ζ > 0 and every subsequently prescribed inverse accuracy M1, sufficiently high finite transport and Taylor orders yield a real interior tensor hp T and a real exterior tensor hB T with the following properties. Put AT = e−αT , α = 7κ/8, λT = eζT . (4.25) The interior field has the form hp T = AT tr. rev.g Re  eiλT v J X j=0 λ−j T pj   . (4.26) Every fixed normalized coefficient jet of pj is eo(T). The field is supported in a fixed-width neighborhood of v = T, with angular support in the transported launch patch. Its relative array qT = (hp T (êα, êβ)) satisfies ∥qT ∥CN (DT ) ≤ AT λN T eo(T) (4.27) 23 at each specified order. The tensor p0 is trace-free and p0(L0, ·) = 0. There is a purely angular γ-unit vector X at pT for which σT := Re eiλT T p0(X, X)  (4.28) has two-sided subexponential size. The a-scaled linear wave residual and √ a-scaled linear gauge resid- ual, in normalized slots and with all prescribed ordinary derivatives, are bounded by AT λ−M1 T eo(T). In regular exterior lab components, ∥hB T ∥CNb ≤ AT λ Nb+3/2 T eo(T) . (4.29) Its linear wave and gauge residuals, and its difference from hp T on the entry collar, have size AT λ−M1 T eo(T) at all the prescribed finite orders. The latter assertion includes normal spacetime jets. On the original bridge its support lies in Equation (4.11) with arbitrarily thin tube margins. Increasing M1 and the finite formal degrees does not increase the positive frequency powers in Equations (4.27) and (4.29). Thresholds and subexponential constants may depend on those degrees.
